_comment: The only place a post is registered. scripts/build-nav.js regenerates every sidebar and the index from this file, so adding a post is one edit here plus the page itself — not an edit to every page on the site.

labs.title: CDN
labs.blurb: Most explanations stop at "it keeps copies closer to users". That's true and it's not enough to work with. It doesn't tell you why turning a CDN on often caches nothing, why a cache can serve the wrong visitor's content while reporting perfect health, or why clearing your cache can make your site four times slower worldwide.
labs.note: Each post has a Run it live button. Recorded numbers appear instantly; pressing the button fires real requests against a server in Oregon behind Cloudflare.

posts.title: Why distance is the whole problem
posts.blurb: A round trip to Oregon costs ~200ms no matter how fast your code is. What a cache hit actually removes.

posts.title: Turning a CDN on caches nothing
posts.blurb: A textbook-perfect Cache-Control header, and still zero caching. Two decisions that look like one.

posts.title: Every city caches separately
posts.blurb: Warming the cache in Singapore does nothing for Tokyo. Measured across ten cities.

posts.title: How cache keys shatter
posts.blurb: Five people share one link on different platforms and your cache becomes five objects.

posts.title: Fresh, stale, and serving old data on purpose
posts.blurb: The trick that answers in 55ms from a server taking two seconds.

posts.title: The thundering herd
posts.blurb: What happens when every cache empties at once — and which defence protects whom.

labs.title: Rate limiting
labs.blurb: Every limiter answers one question — has this client had too many? — and the obvious way to answer it lets a client take twice its limit without breaking a rule.
labs.note: The algorithms are deterministic arithmetic, so these posts simulate them side by side in your browser with no network involved. Only the last one talks to a server, because being genuinely refused cannot be simulated.

posts.nav: Counting is harder than it looks
posts.title: Counting requests is harder than it looks
posts.blurb: Four different jobs a limiter does, and why the obvious implementation has a hole.

posts.title: The boundary burst
posts.blurb: Twice the limit in two seconds, entirely within the rules. What each fix costs.

posts.title: Token bucket: allowing bursts on purpose
posts.blurb: Real clients are bursty. Separating sustained rate from burst tolerance.

posts.title: Your limit is multiplied by your server count
posts.blurb: Eight servers turn a limit of 10 into a limit of 80. What exactness costs.

posts.title: Saying no properly
posts.blurb: A bare 429 causes the traffic it was meant to stop. Trip a real limiter yourself.
